team.name: Dr. Chantelle Recsky
team.bio: Dr. Recsky is a Registered Nurse and her areas of interest include health information technologies, quality and safety, and knowledge translation, as well as supporting students to gain knowledge and experience in research.

team.name: Andrea Burrows
team.bio: Andrea is a Registered Nurse and PhD candidate in the Faculty of Health and Social Development at the University of British Columbia, Okanagan Campus. Her doctoral research explores how nurses use digital technologies to provide individualised care for families in enhanced family visiting programs from across Canada. Andrea holds a Masters of Science in Nursing from UBC and a Bachelors of Science in Nursing from the University of Alberta. Outside her research, Andrea enjoys spending time with her family.

team.name: Naureen Mukhi
team.bio: Naureen Mukhi is a Registered Nurse and Graduate Research Assistant working on her Masters in Nursing at the University of British Columbia (Okanagan). Her thesis is on investigating health system stakeholders' perspectives use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for clinical decision support. Naureen has completed her diploma in Digital Health and Data Analytics from the Michener Institute of Education in Ontario. In parallel with her studies, she also works as Digital Health Clinical Lead at Royal Columbian Hospital with Fraser Health in BC. Naureen enjoys nature, running and spends time volunteering in her community prayer place.

team.name: Josephine Nanyonjo
team.bio: Josephine is deeply committed to addressing the persistent health inequities that exist globally. As a Registered Nurse, she has dedicated the past few years to improving healthcare in rural and underserved areas of Uganda, utilizing her knowledge, skills, and time to make a tangible impact. She is particularly enthusiastic about the potential of technology to provide innovative solutions to this enduring global challenge. Josephine is a social person who values spending time with friends and family, and enjoys swimming, hiking and spending time in nature.

team.name: Jianan Wang
team.bio: Jianan is a nursing PhD student from Zhejiang University, China, and is currently a visiting international research student at UBCO. She received her B.S. in Nursing from Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, China. Her research focuses on the ethical implications of information technology in the nursing field, with a particular interest in understanding how these technologies influence nurses' behaviors.

team.name: Dr. Hilal Yıldırım
team.role: Visiting Scientist, Associate Professor ( Inonu University, Türkiye)
team.bio: Dr Hilal Yıldırım is a Visiting Scientist at the University of British Columbia Okanagan, working under the supervision of Charlene Ronquillo, whose work in digital health and health equity has been highly influential in shaping her current research direction. She is an Associate Professor in the Department of Public Health Nursing at Inonu University, Türkiye, where she continues her academic and research activities. Dr. Yıldırım has been actively engaged in academia since 2011, following her clinical experience in hospital settings between 2009 and 2011. With over a decade of experience, her work focuses on public health nursing, social determinants of health, and vulnerable populations, with a growing emphasis on healthy aging and equitable access to care. Her current research centers on digital health and remote care technologies for older adults, particularly in disaster-affected and resource-constrained settings. She is especially interested in how innovative, technology-supported approaches can enhance accessibility, usability, and continuity of care for aging populations within community and public health systems.

team.name: Nicole Ketter
team.bio: Nicole is currently an MD student in UBC’s Island Medical Program. She previously completed her BSc in Biology from UBCO and her MSc in Rehabilitation Sciences from UBC. She has been part of the HIE lab since 2022 and enjoys contributing to developing knowledge on responsible AI use.

team.name: Diana Shim
team.bio: Diana Shim is a third-year nursing student at UBC Okanagan. She has clinical experience as an Employed Student Nurse, has contributed to the Interior Health New Grad Steering Committee, and has supported students as a simulation lab monitor. She is excited to develop her skills in academic writing, literature reviews, qualitative research, and technology-enabled equity work. Outside of academics, Diana enjoys spending time with friends, baking, and cooking.

pieIntro: Patient/Provider/Process Involvement Engagement — the HIE lab's standing group of patient partners, providers and process advisors. Long-term members who shape research questions, priorities, study design and knowledge translation across all of our work, keeping it grounded in lived experience and real-world practice.

pie.name: Lyn Brooks
pie.focus: Founder of dHub Group, eMHIC Ambassador, and a member of the AI Ethics Advisory Panel at Canada’s Digital Governance Council. Advocates for data sovereignty by design, community data commons and platform cooperativism.

pie.name: Chris J
pie.focus: Lifelong experience of complex chronic illness, brought to research, quality improvement, health technology assessment, standards development and governance. Background in instructional design and web technologies; interests in AI, interoperability and health data literacy.

pie.name: Katie Tong
pie.focus: Navigates a chronic health condition while also a parent and a caregiver to elderly parents. A corporate tech team lead by profession, a patient partner since 2019, and committed to research that weighs lived experience equally with evidence.

pie.name: Michel White
pie.focus: Twenty-five years as a patient partner across dozens of committees, including the Physician Quality Improvement steering committee. Lives with panhypopituitarism and is a transplant caregiver. Speaks for patients who cannot or do not know how to speak for themselves.

speaking.intro: I speak on AI, equity and nursing practice — keynotes, rounds, panels, workshops and board education. What I charge depends on who is asking and what the work is.
speaking.scaleNote: Four bands rather than a price list. Community and patient-led work is unpaid by design and subsidised by the commercial band; if a fee is the only barrier, say so in your message and I will find a way.
topics: Participatory design with patients and providers
AI and the future of health research and training

tiers.who: Patient-led and community organisations, volunteer-run nursing chapters, student societies, public libraries, K-12 and undergraduate classes.
tiers.detail: In person: travel and accommodation coverage. Two of these a term, first come.

tiers.who: Universities, hospital rounds and grand rounds, non-profit research conferences, professional associations, health charities.
tiers.detail: Virtual talks sit at the lower end of the range, in-person keynotes at the upper.

tiers.who: Health authorities, provincial and federal ministries, Crown agencies, accreditation, regulatory and standards bodies.
tiers.detail: Virtual and in-person keynotes are quoted separately. Half-day workshops and facilitated sessions sit above both.

tiers.who: Vendors, consultancies, for-profit conferences, sponsored webinars and podcasts, commercial advisory boards.
tiers.detail: Keynotes, workshops, advisory days and hourly consultations are each quoted on request.

notes.head: What moves the number
notes.body: A talk built from scratch or requiring new analysis carries a supplement · extra sessions, panels or media on the same day are charged as additional work · recording kept and redistributed by the host: licensed separately · multi-day facilitation quoted as a day rate.

notes.head: Travel and logistics
notes.body: Fees exclude travel. In person: economy airfare, accommodation, ground transport and a per diem, booked by the host or reimbursed · cross-country and international bookings need a day either side · virtual is often the better use of everyone's budget.

notes.head: Booking
notes.body: Six to eight weeks' notice preferred · commercial bookings confirm on a deposit, with the balance due after the event · cancellation inside two weeks is invoiced at half

join.openHead: Not accepting graduate students for the 2027 intakes.
join.body: Across every level of collaboration and supervision I encourage applicants from groups underrepresented in nursing research and academia. Note: I do not take on supervision inquiries made within one month of an application deadline.

columns.head: Send me
columns.body: A short note on the project you want to work on and how your background fits · your informatics background and any publications · unofficial transcripts · CV and a writing sample.
columns.foot: Attach these to the form and they reach me directly.

columns.head: PhD applicants
columns.body: A foundational grounding in nursing or health informatics · a completed Masters in nursing, informatics or a related field · at least one peer-reviewed paper in a health informatics journal.
columns.foot: UBC IGS Global Studies / UBCO Nursing Grad

columns.head: Everyone else
columns.body: Postdocs, local or remote. Health authorities, NGOs, community organisations and industry working on health equity and health technology. UBCO nursing students wanting a Y4 preceptorship.

about.kicker: Filipina scholar · Registered nurse · Health informatician
about.lead: Our work is interdisciplinary and underpinned by critical theories, implementation science, and complex systems thinking. Aimed at meaningful inclusion of non-dominant groups in how health technologies are conceived, designed, built and implemented.
about.body: Charlene works in mixed methods, participatory and co-production approaches: nursing AI & informatics competencies, usability research, person-centred design, and technology adoption.
about.funders: Funded by AMS Healthcare, Brocher Foundation, Canadian Nurses Foundation, Roche Canada, SSHRC, and UBC internal grants.
about.researchQuote: Non-dominant groups belong throughout the system development pipeline, not just at the start or evaluation.
about.peopleQuote: Above all we value doing good work with good people — centering humility, compassion, justice, transparency, interdisciplinarity.
